title: The "Combined Experience" Math
reality: 4 founders x 25 years each? LinkedIn reveals: 35 years total. In AI specifically: 4.
example: Apparently time moves differently in startup land.

title: The "Senior Bank Executive"
reality: FINRA shows no registration. LinkedIn reveals "Technology Project Manager" overseeing CRM upgrades.
example: By this logic, the night janitor at Blackrock also "worked with trillions".

title: The Revolutionary Terminology
claim: Financial AGI with Cognitive Knowledge Orchestration (TM)
reality: Google Scholar results: 0. Academic papers: 0. Peer reviews: 0.
example: Invented terminology that sounds impressive precisely because no one can evaluate it.

title: The Impressive Case Study
claim: A leading biotech consortium reduced timelines by 73%
reality: "Which consortium?" -> "Confidential." "Can we speak to them?" -> "They prefer not to be contacted."
example: The only thing verifiable is that someone typed "73%."

title: The AI-Generated Business Plan
claim: Operationalizing cross-functional synergies through AI-native methodologies
reality: This sentence could describe any software. Or a toaster. Or nothing at all.
example: Pro tip: If you can replace "AI" with "blockchain" and it still works, it says nothing.

title: The Exclusive Demo
claim: Sign this NDA, provide sample data, then we'll schedule a preliminary discussion
reality: Translation: "Limit demos" = no working demo. "NDA required" = legal cover for nothing.
example: Real platforms: "Here's a sandbox, try it yourself."

title: The Double Trademark
reality: That's not how trademarks work. One ™ means unregistered claim. Two means nobody proofread... or nobody cares.
example: When even the brand name has a copy-paste error, imagine the codebase.

title: The Round Number Parade
claim: 3x engagement! 60% faster! 40% fewer tickets! 80% faster insights! 90% accuracy!
reality: Five stats, all suspiciously round, zero citations, zero methodology, zero named customers.
example: If your metrics end in 0 and have no source, they came from the marketing meeting, not the data team.

title: The Ghost Testimonial
claim: "100% satisfaction" — Centre Director, Early Learning Centre
reality: No name. No specific organisation. No way to verify. Could be the founder's mum.
example: Real testimonials have real names and real companies that you can actually Google.

title: The Circular Proof
claim: Try our AI demo — ask it about our platform!
reality: The demo proves itself by... talking about itself. That's not proof, that's a chatbot reading its own marketing page.
example: Asking an AI "are you good?" is like asking a used car if it runs well.

title: The Trust Mirage
claim: Trusted Across Industries — Education, Healthcare, Legal, Research...
reality: Eight industries claimed. Zero named organisations. Zero logos. Zero case studies. Just a grid of icons.
example: 'Trusted' by whom? By the designer who made the icons, apparently.

title: The Phantom App
claim: Download on the App Store / Get it on Google Play
reality: App store links on the website but... have you actually searched for it? Is it there? Does it have reviews?
example: Pro tip: Always check the store listing independently. Linking isn't shipping.

title: The 2-Minute Miracle
claim: 2 Minutes to Go Live — start chatting instantly!
reality: Enterprise AI platform with security, analytics, multi-language support, role-based permissions... live in 2 minutes?
example: If setup takes 2 minutes, support will take 2 years.

title: The Enterprise Facade
claim: Enterprise Security — multi-layered protection, access control, organizational isolation
reality: No SOC 2 mentioned. No ISO 27001. No penetration test results. No audit reports. Just adjectives.
example: 'Enterprise-grade' without a certification number is just a font size.
